title: Lobster Bisque
description: Rich and flavorful Lobster Bisque is an easy recipe to make at home. This bisque is the best chance for a home cook to shine. Adapted from the recipe of the Carlyle’s executive chef, it contains one of the great kitchen cheats of all time: a method for imparting rich creaminess that in a lesser establishment would come from a roux of butter and flour or a handful of cornstarch. You may end up using it all the time.
directions: Split lobster tails lengthwise with sharp kitchen shears. Remove meat and set aside (saving shells).
Heat butter over medium heat in a large pot. Add the onions, carrots, and celery. Stir to coat in butter and cook until soft, about 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add garlic and tomato paste, and cook for 1 minute.
Deglaze the pot by filling with about 4 cups of liquid: 1 cup sherry or white wine, 2 cups seafood stock and 1 cup water.
Add empty shells to pot, then the Herbes de Provence and a teaspoon of salt. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce heat as low, simmering slightly covered for about 20 minutes.

Add the lobster meat, cover with lid, and let simmer for 5 minutes. Remove when meat is bright red and white. If any part is still translucent, continue to simmer until cooked. Remove meat from pot and transfer to a cutting board. Cut into small pieces and refrigerate until ready to add to bisque.
Strain the broth through a colander, wipe out the pot, and pour the broth back in. Add the ½ cup rice and cook for at least 30 minutes, or until the grains are cooked to extreme softness.

Blend the bisque in a food processor or immersion blender, then pass through a fine sieve, pressing down hard on what solids remain. (You can stop here and refrigerate, if you’re making it ahead of time.)

When ready to serve, add the cream and bring to a low simmer. Add chopped lobster meat, let it heat through, seasoning to taste with salt (maybe some cayenne or pepper, maybe adding some snipped chives).
